name: sunny-g1-transport-feasibility-g0

sources.title: HttpListener.GetContextAsync
sources.claim: Completes when an incoming request has been received; not documented as a first-byte or partial-header event.

sources.title: HttpListenerRequest.RawUrl
sources.claim: URL part after domain; includes query; does not document original Host/header wire multiplicity or pre-handler evidence.

sources.title: HttpListener.Abort
sources.claim: Shuts down listener immediately, discarding queued requests; not per-request task/buffer completion proof.

sources.title: HttpListenerResponse.Abort
sources.claim: Closes response/context and client connection; does not independently prove pending app ReadAsync completion.

sources.title: ASP.NET Core HTTP.sys server options
sources.claim: Has MaxConnections, RequestQueueLimit and TimeoutManager; availability/enforceability under isolated non-elevated setup unverified.

sources.title: HTTP.sys TimeoutManager.HeaderWait
sources.claim: HeaderWait only enforced after first request on connection routed to application; first-request slow-header protection not established.

sources.title: HTTP.sys TimeoutManager
sources.claim: EntityBody timer resets upon more data indications, so not a monotonic whole-ingress deadline; RequestQueue limit separate.

sources.title: Kestrel server options
sources.claim: RequestHeadersTimeout, MaxConcurrentConnections, body size and rate limits documented; not a verified total first-byte deadline.

sources.title: Kestrel limits and security considerations
sources.claim: Header total/count and request-line limits documented; settings not automatically equal raw-wire fidelity.

sources.title: ASP.NET Core IHttpRequestFeature
sources.claim: RawTarget and header value arrays exposed as features; not a guarantee of byte-for-byte raw Host/duplicate line syntax after parsing.

sources.title: ASP.NET Core IHttpConnectionFeature
sources.claim: Local/remote IP/port and ConnectionId exposed; server provenance still must be verified.

sources.title: ASP.NET Core HttpContext.Abort
sources.claim: Aborts connection underlying request; does not guarantee observed completion of an uncooperative application task.

sources.title: TcpListener.Start/Stop
sources.claim: Stopping listener does not close accepted connections; custom parser/connection/buffer ownership risk remains.

rules: All five G1E-02..06 required properties need independently reviewed method, before G1E-01 design can close; any unknown mandatory safety property BLOCKS transport selection
HeaderWait enforced after first routed request does not establish first-request slow-header protection
HTTP.sys EntityBody idle timer resets upon data and cannot substitute for a nonresetting monotonic total ingress deadline
Client-written raw bytes do not prove server/HTTP.sys reception; API request-target/header features do not imply preserved original wire Host syntax
HttpContext.Abort/HttpListenerResponse.Abort/HttpListener.Abort and socket Stop are lifecycle requests, not proof of pending application task completion
Only source-backed feasibility documented here; real Windows measurements, numeric approval and user/operator permission remain future work
Custom TcpListener parser is a high-risk alternative requiring full independent parsing/framing review; never a production recommendation from this document
